findings.claim: After 24 weeks, abortion is only permitted if the mother’s life is at risk or the foetus has a severe abnormality.
findings.truth: Three grounds of the Abortion Act 1967 have no time limit, not two. Section 1(1)(b) also allows termination at any stage when it is necessary to prevent grave permanent injury to the physical or mental health of the pregnant woman, alongside 1(1)(c) risk to her life and 1(1)(d) serious foetal abnormality. The word 'only' makes the two-item list a wrong statement of the law.
findings.evidence: legislation.gov.uk, Abortion Act 1967 s.1(1)(a)-(d) as amended by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Act 1990

findings.claim: Many scientists are religious — Pope Francis accepted evolution, showing science and faith can coexist.
findings.truth: Pope Francis was not a scientist, so he is not an example of a religious scientist. The 2014 evolution quotation itself is correct. The real example of a religious scientist in this topic is Georges Lemaître, the Belgian Catholic priest who proposed the expanding universe in 1927 and the 'primeval atom' (the Big Bang) in 1931.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Georges Lemaître (ordained 1923; 1927 expanding-universe paper; 1931 primeval atom)

findings.claim: the sequence in Genesis (light, sky, land, plants, animals, humans) broadly matches the scientific order of events
findings.truth: Genesis 1 places plants on day 3, before the sun, moon and stars on day 4, and birds on day 5 before land animals on day 6. That order does not match the scientific sequence. The claim is written as an argument non-literal Christians make, and the abbreviated list quietly drops day 4, so it is not asserted as fact by the lesson.

findings.claim: There are different types: voluntary euthanasia ..., non-voluntary euthanasia ..., and assisted suicide (helping someone end their own life).
findings.truth: Assisted suicide is a distinct act, not a type of euthanasia: the person ends their own life with help, rather than another person ending it. GCSE resources commonly group the three together, and the legal claim that follows is right, so no edit is made. The lesson also omits the active/passive distinction.
findings.evidence: Suicide Act 1961 s.2; standard GCSE RS terminology

summary: Scripture, hadith, Catechism 2270 and 2417, Laudato Si', the 120-day ensoulment view, Qur'an 51:47 (verbatim Clear Quran) and the 1,1,4,6,12 theme question structure all check out. Two mark-affecting fixes: an incomplete statement of the post-24-week abortion grounds, and a 12-mark mark scheme that offers Pope Francis as an example of a religious scientist.
